sentences.text:
2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that applicant and the victim/prosecutrix are resident of same village and on the pretext of marriage, applicant sexually exploited her for about two months;
subsequently, the applicant refused to marry her, therefore, present FIR was registered against him and the applicant was arrested on Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28517 24.06.2023.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant would submit that applicant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question, as he has not committed the alleged crime.

He further submits that victim/prosecutrix is major lady and she is consenting party to the act of the applicant; and the report was lodged by her against the applicant only because he refused to marry her.

He would further submit that the applicant is in jail since 24.06.2023; charge-sheet has already been filed and conclusion of the trial is likely to take considerable time, hence, the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
5. I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties, having regard to the facts &
circumstances of the case; particularly considering pri-trial detention of the applicant; charge-sheet has already been filed and trial is likely to take long time for its final disposal; this Court is of the view that it is a fit case to release the applicants on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
7. Accused/applicant is directed to be released on bail on his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
He is directed to appear Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:28517 before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.

Sd/-
(Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi) Judge Amit/-
